rawItems.title: Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan 2026-2046 Examination Report Published
rawItems.meetingTitle: Independent Examiner's Report for Huntingdonshire District Council and Ramsey Town Council
rawItems.summary: An independent examination of the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan 2026-2046 has concluded that the Plan meets the Basic Conditions, subject to recommended policy modifications. The report, dated 25 August 2026, recommends that the modified Plan proceeds to a referendum. It confirms the Plan was prepared by Ramsey Town Council for the designated Ramsey Neighbourhood Plan Area, covers the period 2026-2046, and addresses the development and use of land.

items.title: Reform councillor complains to Parliament over MP’s response to 199-home plan
items.content: A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury. Cllr Karan Maheshwari, who represents Ramsey on Huntingdonshire District Council, has submitted a complaint to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. It concerns North West Cambridgeshire MP Mr Carling’s response to Cllr Maheshwari’s request for him to intervene in planning application 25/01382/OUT, for 199 homes between Ramsey and Bury. A copy seen by this publication is dated November 2 and marked “DRAFT – NOT SUBMITTED”, but Cllr Maheshwari later confirmed he submitted it on November 3 and received confirmation on November 4. The dispute began after Huntingdonshire District Council’s development management committee said it was minded to reject the scheme. items.title: Here is some of Huntingdonshire's most unusual bridges and where to find them
items.content: From a medieval bridge with its own chapel to a 55-arch causeway, Huntingdonshire is packed with unusual crossings. The district’s rivers, floodplains and Fenland waterways have shaped travel for centuries, leaving medieval crossings and Fen drainage bridges behind. Here are some of Huntingdonshire’s most striking bridges and where to find them. St Ives Bridge One of the county’s most extraordinary bridges spans the River Great Ouse at St Ives. The town’s first bridge was built of wood in 1107, before work began on a stone replacement in the early 15th century. The stone crossing was completed in 1425, and a chapel was added the following year. It is one of only three bridges in England with a chapel. The bridge also still bears the scars of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops destroyed part of it to hinder Royalist forces, so a temporary drawbridge was installed. When the damaged section was rebuilt in 1716, it was given rounded arches instead of matching the pointed medieval ones, leaving a visible difference today. items.title: Hunts man due in court accused of employee theft and fraud offences named
items.content: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court. He is alleged to have spent £935.83 on personal items using a company credit card while on leave between August 21 and September 2, knowing the transactions were unauthorised and intending to make financial gain. He is also accused of stealing an Apple iPhone worth £285, a Lenovo laptop worth £478 and several tools, including a drill set. The items belonged to water treatment supplier Prodose Ltd and were allegedly stolen between September 2 and October 14. Between November 13 and December 8, Mr Stokes is accused of stealing tools valued at £2,109.18 from Riverside Waste Machinery Ltd. A further fraud charge alleges that he used or permitted the use of company credit cards for unauthorised transactions totalling £412.41 between October 6 and December 8. All the offences are alleged to have taken place in Huntingdon.

items.title: Plans submitted for four-caravan traveller site on land near Ramsey
items.content: Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home." items.title: Town Council Vacancies Due to Councillor Resignations
items.summary: Notice given of two council vacancies following the resignations of Councillor Ash Austin and Councillor Phil Rose. An election will be held if requested in writing by ten electors within 14 statutory days to the Returning Officer at Huntingdonshire District Council; otherwise, the Town Council will fill the vacancies by co-option.

items.title: Planning Application 3226/01526/FUL - Temporary Retail/Community Space on Great Whyte
items.summary: The Council considered an application for temporary permission (15 years) for 3 units of retail/community space and highway improvements on the Pedestrian Island, Great Whyte. An amended motion stating there was insufficient information to support the application was passed (5 for, 3 against, 6 abstentions).

items.title: Planning Application 25/01301/FUL - Riverside Lake and Leisure, Mereside Drove
items.summary: The Council voted unanimously to recommend approval for the erection of an owner/site manager's dwelling, retention of 14 touring caravan pitches, toilet/shower block, 3 holiday lodges, plus the addition of two new timber holiday lodges and four holiday pods.

items.title: Planning Application 26/01763/FUL - Oak Cottage, Forty Foot Bank
items.summary: The Council voted by majority (6 for, 8 against, 1 abstention) to recommend refusal for the erection of 3 detached dwellings, 3 detached double garages, and associated works, echoing concerns raised by neighbouring residents.

items.title: Planning Application 26/01763/FUL/26/01764/LBC - Bodsey House, Bodsey Toll Road
items.summary: The Council voted unanimously to recommend approval for the proposed conversion and extension of an existing curtilage-listed outbuilding into a separate dwellinghouse.

items.title: Planning Application Recommendations and Updates
items.summary: Council to discuss several planning applications including temporary permission for retail/community space on Great Whyte, holiday park expansions at Mereside Drove, residential developments at Forty Foot Bank and Bodsey Toll Road, and a self-build appeal at Bucks Drove.

items.title: Planning Application Recommendation: 199 Dwellings off Stoneman Way and Biggin Lane
items.summary: Council voted unanimously to recommend refusal for outline application 25/01382/OUT due to incorrect speed limits in the traffic assessment, coalescence concerns between Bury Village and Ramsey Town, and inadequate drainage flowing into Slade Dyke.

items.title: Planning Application Recommendation: Two Drive-Thru Units on St Marys Road
items.summary: Council voted unanimously to recommend approval for application 26/00681/FUL for the construction of 2 drive-thru units with landscaping at Plot 09A St Marys Road, Ramsey.

items.title: Planning Application Query: Open Storage of Vehicles at Factory Bank
items.summary: Council voted 11 for and 1 abstention to defer a formal vote on application 26/01584/FUL pending further information regarding agricultural land change of use, environmental contamination, drainage, and encroachment on the Northern Gateway MUGA site.

items.title: Planning Application Recommendation: Variation of Condition at Oilmills Road, Ramsey Mereside
items.summary: Council voted unanimously to recommend approval for application 26/01670/S73 (variation of condition 2 for Land Rear of 192 Oilmills Road).

items.title: Mews Car Park and Great Whyte Improvements Update
items.summary: The Mayor updated the council on positive discussions regarding the Pedestrianisation Project and a proposed 50-year leasehold for the land behind the doctors on Mews Close for parking, supported by HDC CIL funding applications.

items.title: Planning Application Recommendation: 25/01382/OUT (Stoneman Way and Biggin Lane)
items.summary: Council voted unanimously to recommend refusal for the outline application of up to 199 dwellings due to incorrect speed data in traffic assessments, concerns over coalescence between Bury and Ramsey, and inadequate drainage.

items.title: Planning Application Recommendation: 26/00681/FUL (St Marys Road)
items.summary: Council voted unanimously to recommend approval for the construction of 2 drive-thru units with associated landscaping at Plot 09A St Marys Road.
